81292.subject:
The SEC Just Opened A Door For Tokenization. Real Estate Was Not
 Invited.
81292.body:
Ment Tech | Meant To Innovate

Автор: Ment Tech Labs


Автор: Ment Tech Labs

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення
Прочитати на LinkedIn
https://www.linkedin.com/comm/pulse/sec-just-opened-door-tokenization-real-estate-invited-menttechlabs-mtcjf?lipi=urn%3Ali%3Apage%3Aemail_email_series_follow_newsletter_02%3BBWIfcxsER9aNzMyXbrKmfA%3D%3D&midToken=AQFTjFOONAfT2w&midSig=1_z1ftfWZrWYs1&trk=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_&trkEmail=eml-email_series_follow_newsletter_02-null-0-read_more_banner_cta_-null-fz96fz~mvkrsugq~2f-null-null&eid=fz96fz-mvkrsugq-2f
  
Two days ago, on October 20, 2026, a comment window closed in Washington that almost nobody in real estate was watching. The SEC had proposed Regulation Crypto Assets back in August, a tailored offering framework for crypto assets. Crypto media called it the green light. Threads went up. "The SEC finally opened the door." Then came the part nobody quoted. The proposal reaches only investment contracts involving a non-security crypto asset and nothing else. A token tied to a building, a commodity, or a royalty stream falls entirely outside it. Your property token was never in scope. If you are sitting on real assets and waiting for Washington to make tokenization simple, that wait just got longer. Meanwhile, one Gulf government has been running a live tokenized property market for over a year. What the SEC Actually Said, and What It Did Not Three separate things happened in 2026, and the market keeps collapsing them into one. They are not the same. Read the last column down the table. Not one of those three created a new route for a tokenized building. The SEC's position has been consistent and it is worth stating plainly: moving an activity on-chain does not move it outside the securities laws. So How Do You Actually Tokenize Property In The US? The same way you did before any of this. Through exemptions that have existed for decades. Regulation D 506(c). Permits broad advertising, restricts buyers to accredited investors Regulation S. Capital raises outside the US with no SEC registration, as long as US persons are excluded Regulation A+. Opens the door to non-accredited investors, with lower raise ceilings and more disclosure Transfer agent oversight, accredited checks, resale restrictions. Not optional extras. The structure itself Most serious platforms run Reg D and Reg S together, reaching domestic accredited investors and global buyers at the same time. There is no shortcut arriving. There is only whether your token model was designed to fit these rules or bolted onto them afterward. The Market Did Not Wait For Clarity While the frameworks argue with each other, the money moved. 81070.subject: 💰 The Funding: What happens if MSCI drops crypto treasuries like Strategy?
81070.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/c1c9af72-58d8-47c5-88eb-8e5007f7e3dc/unnamed__17_.png?t=1789144554)
Caption: 

Written by Yogita Khatri  | Edited by Zack Abrams

———————————————————————————

Presented By:

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/0f002faa-88b1-4362-8467-fbc25a6c61ee/Screenshot_2026-10-16_at_4.02.56_PM__3___1___1___1_.png?t=1792184177)
Caption: 

———————————————————————————

----------
Happy Sunday, and welcome to the 62nd edition of [The Funding](https://www.theblock.co/newsletters/the-funding)!

MSCI [finalized rules](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-10-15-msci-rules-could-exclude-strategy-mstr-from-indexes-418729) on Oct. 15 that could push Strategy and other crypto treasury companies out of its main global indexes as soon as Nov. 30. What would that mean for how these companies raise money, and is anyone still willing to fund them? I caught up with investors and analysts to find out.

Let's get into it.


----------———————————————————————————

----------
# THE INSIDE VIEW

## What if MSCI drops crypto treasuries?


----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2012e140-bc90-4ae9-b029-9f403353161b/Dat-Image-1200x675.jpg?t=1792371900)
Caption: 

----------
Index provider MSCI recently [approved new rules](https://app2.msci.com/webapp/index_ann/DocGet?pub_key=aq0wbkjxPgo%3D&lang=en&format=html) that target "non-operating" companies, which mainly hold assets instead of running a business, such as digital asset treasury firms, or DATs.

Under the new rules, MSCI will first check whether a company has substantial operating assets, such as equipment or inventory. In the [proposal MSCI published in August](https://www.msci.com/downloads/documents/indexes/consultations/equity/Consultation%20on%20Eligibility%20of%20Non-Operating%20Companies%20for%20the%20%20MSCI%20Global%20Investable%20Market%20Indexes.pdf), that meant operating assets making up more than half of total assets. Companies that fail this check face five financial tests, which in the proposal included whether a company generates operating cash flow and how much it relies on raising capital to buy assets. Those flagged on four or more will be excluded.

Current index members get some leeway: they will be removed only if they fail in both of their two most recent annual filing periods. If they fail in only one, they stay in the index unless they fail the following year. Companies not yet in the index are blocked if they fail in either of the last two years.

In a simulation published in August using May data, MSCI flagged two bitcoin treasury companies, Michael Saylor's Strategy and Japan's Metaplanet, for potential exclusion. Ethereum treasury firm SharpLink
